 No Botox, No Plastic Surgery: Julianne Moore, 65, Swears by
These 3 Skincare Ingredients to Keep Her Mature Skin Glowing
 At 65, Julianne Moore swears by three simple skincare
essentials to keep her complexion radiant, healthy, and
glowing.
American actress Julianne Moore at Rome Film Fest 2026, The Debut
Red carpet, Rome (Italy), October 21st, 2026 (Photo by Massimo
Insabato/Archivio Massimo Insabato/Mondadori Portfolio via Getty
Images) 
 The internet loves to act shocked that Julianne Moore is 65, as
if she has discovered a secret portal to 1998. Her face tells a
different story: freckles, expression lines, and that calm,
expensive-looking glow that reads more “well rested” than
“overfilled.”
 Her routine for mature skin is not a 14-step spreadsheet of
acids. It is a tight little system built around three serious
ingredients, a lifelong sunscreen habit, and the kind of
consistency most of us only bring to streaming shows.
 Why Julianne Moore Is The Gold Standard For Mature Skin
 Moore is a worst-case scenario on paper: very fair, freckled,
burns just by looking at a beach. Dermatologists will tell you that
skin like that usually shows sun damage early, with spots, sagging,
and a rough texture by midlife. Instead, at 65, she is the woman
other women Google to figure out what is humanly possible after
50.
 Her advantage is not “good genes and green juice.” She has
talked about avoiding sun from a young age, building her life
around hats, shade, and daily SPF. She also refuses the panic
language of “anti-aging,” preferring to keep her face expressive
and her skin healthy rather than frozen. The strategy is classic:
protect, treat, moisturize. The discipline is very Julianne.
 The 3-Step “Holy Trinity” Behind Her Glow
 Moore credits her facialist, Fabricio Ormonde, with simplifying
everything into a mature-skin power trio. I follow my facialist
Fabricio Ormonde’s instructions: a daytime vitamin C serum, retinol
and a neck cream, Moore says.
 Step one is vitamin C in the morning. She reaches for iS
Clinical Pro-Heal Serum Advance+, a serious antioxidant that acts
like a shield against pollution and UV stress while helping with
collagen support and dark spots. On fair, freckled skin that loves
to pigment, vitamin C is damage control in a bottle. She layers it
under her daily sunscreen, a lightweight 
SPF 50 like Biore UV Aqua Rich Watery Essence, so protection
and glow work together instead of fighting for space.
 At night, the spotlight moves to retinol. Moore uses Environ
Youth EssentiA Vita-Peptide C-Quence Serum 3, which pairs vitamin A
derivatives with peptides to encourage collagen and smoother
texture. Retinol speeds up cell turnover, softens lines, and helps
re-firm slack areas, which is exactly what mature skin starts to
lose after menopause. If you are copying her, think slow and
gentle: start retinol two nights a week, apply a plain moisturizer
first if you are sensitive, and skip the harsh scrubs.
 The third non-negotiable is neck cream. Most people stop at the
jaw and then act surprised when their neck tells a different age.
Moore uses Revision Skincare Nectifirm Advanced, a rich formula
built for the thinner, drier skin on the neck and décolletage. The
goal is harmony – no smooth, lifted face sitting on a crepey neck.
And floating over all of it is the invisible fourth step she has
stuck to for decades: broad-spectrum SPF, every single morning, no
matter what.
 How To Adapt Julianne’s Routine To Your Own Mature Skin
 You do not need her exact products or her facialist on speed
dial. Think in functions, not logos: a gentle cleanse, an
antioxidant in the morning, a retinoid at night, serious sunscreen,
and something nurturing for the neck. That is the Julianne
blueprint, whether you are at a luxury counter or in the drugstore
aisle.
 Morning: Wash with a mild, non-foaming
cleanser. Moore reaches for Cetaphil-type formulas that do not
leave skin tight.
 Apply a vitamin C serum to face, neck, and chest. Look for
opaque or tinted packaging and a comfortable texture rather than
chasing the highest percentage.
 Follow with a basic moisturizer if you are dry, then a
dedicated neck or firming cream, bringing everything down over the
collarbones.
 Finish with a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher that you actually
enjoy applying. A thin, watery gel like her Biore favorite is ideal
if you hate heavy creams.
 Night: Cleanse again, gently. Skip aggressive
scrubs; Moore uses a soft textured towel for the 
lightest exfoliation .
 On retinol nights, apply a pea-sized amount to dry skin,
avoiding the corners of the nose and mouth, then seal with
moisturizer and your neck cream. On off nights, just load up on
hydration.
 If you have a deeper skin tone, the playbook is almost
identical. Hyperpigmentation may show up as patches rather than
freckles, but vitamin C, retinol, and religious sunscreen are still
your best friends. What changes is shade of foundation, not how
hard UV rays hit. For very reactive or dry skin, slow the pace:
retinol once a week at first, plenty of bland moisturizer, and skip
layering other strong acids in the same routine.
